packages.label: עֲמָלֵק, פִילוֹסוֹפִים וְאֶבֶן נֶגֶף
packages.label_en: Amalek, Philosophers, and the Stumbling Block
packages.reason: Amalek, the philosophers-and-heretics, and the stumbling block embedded in each of the seven wisdoms are all different expressions of the same evil reality: philosophical inquiry that operates by natural reason alone, denies God, and thereby causes spiritual downfall. The Rebbe makes this identity explicit in both directions: 'עֲמָלֵק, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת הַפִילוֹסוֹפִים וְהַכּוֹפְרִים' and 'יֵשׁ אֶבֶן נֶגֶף בְּכָל חָכְמָה וְחָכְמָה, שֶׁהִיא בְּחִינַת עֲמָלֵק'. The stumbling block (אֶבֶן נֶגֶף) is not a different entity from Amalek — it IS Amalek manifesting within each discipline. The philosophers and heretics are not a different entity from Amalek — they ARE Amalek in its contemporary expression. All three share the same essential nature: the anti-faith intellectual force that denies fear of God and practical commandments.

packages.label: תַּכְלִית וְסוֹף דָּבָר
packages.label_en: Ultimate Purpose and the Final Word
packages.reason: The Rebbe explicitly states: 'עִקָּר הַשָּׂגַת הַתַּכְלִית, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת סוֹף דָּבָר'. The verse from Kohelet — 'סוֹף דָּבָר הַכֹּל נִשְׁמָע' — is not merely an illustration of the concept of telos; the Rebbe identifies it as the same thing. Both concepts point to the identical reality: the ultimate endpoint and summation of existence, which is achieved through simplicity and fear of God. תַּכְלִית (telos/ultimate purpose) and סוֹף דָּבָר (the final word/conclusion of all things) are two names for the same essential nature — the completion and culmination of all human effort and spiritual aspiration.
